title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Patent Adjudication Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Patent Trial Work

(February 16, 1985)

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the Chinese People's Liberation Army; the Railway Transport High Court; the Intermediate People's Courts of the seats of the people's governments of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; and the Intermediate People's Courts of all Special Economic Zones:

Following the promulgation of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, all High People's Courts and relevant Intermediate People's Courts have organized trial personnel to carefully study the Patent Law and have actively made preparations for its implementation. The Patent Law will come into effect as of April 1 this year. We hereby notify you of several issues concerning the conduct of patent trial work as follows:

(I) Trial Work Concerning Patent Dispute Cases

1. Scope of Case Acceptance

According to the provisions of the Patent Law and its Implementing Regulations, the following seven categories of patent cases shall be tried by the Economic Divisions of the People's Courts:

(1) Disputes over whether an invention patent right should be granted;
(2) Disputes over the invalidation or maintenance of a granted invention patent right;
(3) Disputes over the grant of a compulsory license;
(4) Disputes over the fee for a compulsory license;
(5) Disputes over the fee for the use of an invention, utility model, or design after the publication of the patent application but before the grant of the patent right;
(6) Disputes over patent infringement (including cases of passing off the patent of another person that do not yet constitute a crime);
(7) Disputes over contracts for the assignment of the right to apply for a patent or the patent right.

2. Case Jurisdiction

Based on the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the Patent Law, and its Implementing Regulations, as well as the current actual circumstances, the jurisdiction over patent dispute cases is stipulated as follows:

(1) For categories 1 to 4 in the scope of case acceptance above, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court shall serve as the court of first instance, and the Beijing High People's Court shall serve as the court of second instance.
(2) For categories 5 to 7 in the scope of case acceptance above within each province, autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government, and Special Economic Zone, the Intermediate People's Court of the seat of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and the Intermediate People's Court of each Special Economic Zone, shall respectively serve as the court of first instance, and the High People's Court of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall serve as the court of second instance.

When necessary, a High People's Court of a province or autonomous region may, with the consent of the Supreme People's Court, designate an Intermediate People's Court in an open city within its province or autonomous region, or in a larger city that has a patent administrative authority, as the court of first instance for trying categories 5 to 7 cases within its jurisdiction, as set forth above.

3. Procedural Rules

When hearing various types of patent dispute cases, the People's Courts shall follow the procedural rules provided in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) and the Patent Law. However, two issues need to be clarified:

(1) In disputes over whether an invention patent right should be granted, and disputes over the invalidation or maintenance of a granted invention patent right, the Patent Reexamination Board shall be the defendant. In disputes over the grant of a compulsory license, the Patent Office of the People's Republic of China shall be the defendant. In disputes over fees for compulsory licenses, patent infringement, and fees for the use of inventions, utility models, or designs after publication of the patent application but before the grant of the patent right, where a party is dissatisfied with a ruling or decision made by the Patent Office or a patent administrative authority and files a lawsuit with a People's Court, the parties to the dispute at the time of handling by the Patent Office or the patent administrative authority shall remain the litigants.
(2) In the course of a patent infringement lawsuit, if the defendant counterclaims that the patent right is invalid, the People's Court hearing the patent infringement action shall inform the defendant to proceed in accordance with Articles 48 and 49 of the Patent Law. During this period, the court hearing the patent infringement action may suspend the proceedings pursuant to Article 118(4) of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), and resume the patent infringement action only after the issue of the validity or invalidity of the patent right has been resolved.

4. Promptly Assign Trial Personnel and Utilize the Role of Technical Experts

Patent litigation is a field that closely integrates science and technology with law. It is highly specialized in technical matters and involves a relatively high number of foreign-related cases. Each High and Intermediate People's Court undertaking patent trial tasks shall, based on actual needs, select and assign an appropriate number of trial personnel with some trial experience. Special attention shall be paid to selecting personnel who have studied science or engineering and who understand foreign languages to participate in patent trial work. At a minimum, it shall be possible to form one collegial panel.

When hearing patent cases, the People's Courts shall maintain close contact with relevant departments and give full play to the role of experts and scholars from scientific research institutions and production departments. They may engage them as temporary or permanent technical advisers, appoint them as technical appraisers, or invite them to serve as people's assessors and directly participate in patent trial work.

Patent trial is a new task. The relevant High and Intermediate People's Courts shall organize patent trial personnel to further diligently study the Patent Law and other relevant laws and decrees, and shall pay attention to summarizing the trial experience of patent dispute cases through trial practice.

(II) Trial Work Concerning Criminal Cases Related to Patents

1. For the following three types of acts constituting crimes, criminal liability shall be investigated according to the relevant provisions of the Patent Law and the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China:

(1) Where one passes off the patent of another person, and the circumstances are serious, the person directly responsible shall be punished for the crime of passing off the patent of another person by applying mutatis mutandis Article 127 of the Criminal Law;
(2) Where one violates Article 20 of the Patent Law by filing a patent application abroad without authorization and divulging important state secrets, and the circumstances are serious, the offender shall be punished for the crime of divulging important state secrets in accordance with Article 186 of the Criminal Law;
(3) Where a staff member of the Patent Office or a relevant state staff member engages in favoritism and malpractice, and the circumstances are so serious as to constitute a crime, the offender shall be punished for the crime of favoritism and malpractice by applying mutatis mutandis Article 188 of the Criminal Law.

2. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the three categories of criminal cases mentioned above shall be tried by the Criminal Division of the People's Court having jurisdiction.
